item.title: Volvo CEO Says China Market Gone, Luxury Weakness Remains
item.description:
Volvo plunged by about 30% to a record low after the Swedish automaker’s chief executive officer said the market for Western-developed cars in China is disappearing fast, prompting it to cut 2,500 more jobs.
Luxury powerhouses including Hermès and Cartier are suffering steeper slumps in China, in a sign that a spending pullback by the country’s wealthy consumers is hitting even the most resilient brands.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Rout Slows With Oil Strength Capping Relief: Markets Wrap
item.description: A rout in the artificial intelligence trade faded, offering global stock investors some respite in the final session of a volatile week, with further gains in oil prices keeping sentiment cautious.

item.title: European Stocks Fall as China Woes Hit Volvo Car, Gucci
item.description: European stocks fell for a second day as disappointing earnings, including from Kering SA’s Gucci, added to concerns over the artificial intelligence trade and elevated oil prices.

item.title: Indian Small Caps Post Worst Drop in Five Months on Deleveraging
item.description: A wave of deleveraging by retail investors triggered the biggest rout in Indian small-cap stocks in five months, as mounting concerns over inflation and higher interest rates weigh on sentiment.

item.title: Bolsonaro Trade Faces Reckoning in Too-Close-to-Call Brazil Vote
item.description: Wall Street strategists who recommended loading up on Brazil assets after Flávio Bolsonaro emerged as the frontrunner for president are about to see if they led clients astray or to profits ahead of Sunday’s too-close-to-call runoff.
